text:
For most people, the **JBL Charge 6** is the best overall pick. It's IP68, rugged, has long battery life, and costs about $130–150. If you'll be in or right next to the pool, consider a speaker that **floats**, like the UE Wonderboom 4, UE Epicboom, or JBL Boombox 4.

## Top picks

**1. JBL Charge 6: best all-rounder (~$130–150)**
- IP68 (dust-tight and submersible), 40W, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost). It can also charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi named it best overall. They listed it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon.
- None of these sources says it floats.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) · [BestProducts ($150, 25% off)](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**2. Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4: best budget poolside pick (~$65)**
- IP67, floats, and plays 360° sound. It's softball-sized, rubberized and drop-resistant.
- Battery lasts about 13–14 hours.
- There's no app, and it has less bass than bigger speakers.
- Buy links: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) · [BestProducts ($65)](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**3. Ultimate Ears Epicboom: best 360° party sound**
- IP67 and floats. Sound is consistent from any side of the pool, and it has punchy bass.
- Battery lasts about 15 hours.
- It's Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range pick, but it isn't cheap.
- Buy links: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) · [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**4. JBL Boombox 4: best for big pool or beach parties (premium)**
- RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It handles long immersion, floats, gets loud, and lasts 40+ hours.
- Downsides: it's big and heavy, and it sounds muffled if you're beside or behind it.
- Buy link: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**5. JBL Grip: best light beach-bag speaker (~$100)**
- IP68, weighs under 1 lb, can-shaped, and lasts 12 hours. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester called it the best overall.
- The mesh body traps sand and dust.
- Buy link: [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

**Big party speaker for less: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus ($249.99, or $200 with code)**
- 100W (140W with BassUp), floats, about 20 hours at half volume, and can charge a phone.
- It's heavy at 3.8 kg.
- It's IPX7, which means no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach.
- A deal site reports that code **AFSC20** took $49.99 off in Soundcore's cart on 10/22. That's 20% off full-price items only, valid through 12/31.
- Buy via [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission. You can also go to Soundcore's US store directly and enter the code.

**Tiny budget option:** the [JBL Go 5](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) costs $39.95, is IP67, and lasts about 8 hours.

## Quick buying tips
- **Pool:** look for IP67 or higher, and buy one that floats.
- **Beach:** choose IP6X (dust-tight) so sand stays out. Skip IPX-only models unless you'll keep them on a towel.
- **Care:** IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine corrosion. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use, keep port flaps closed, and let it dry fully before charging ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).

Prices change, so check the retailer's page before buying. If you tell me your budget and whether you care more about portability or loudness, I can narrow this to one pick.
